name: Todo Scan
description: Finds TODO / FIXME / HACK / XXX markers in text the Agent already has, shows them in a dockable panel for triage, and returns what is still open as items or a markdown checklist. Read-only: no file edits, no network.
whenToUse: Use when the user asks to find explicit TODO, FIXME, HACK or XXX markers in code, a diff or notes — "collect the FIXMEs from this PR", "list every HACK before we ship" — or wants to review and tick off marker items in a panel. Matches literal markers only, not plain task lists.

scan_todos.description: Scan text for TODO, FIXME, HACK and XXX markers. Pass the exact text to inspect as `text` (file contents, a diff, or notes); pass `tag` to keep a single marker type. A line may hold several markers: each is reported separately with its 1-based `column`. Returns JSON { total, truncated, scannedLines, byTag, items } where each item is { key, line, column, tag, text }, `line` and `column` being 1-based positions inside the supplied text and `text` the remainder of that line after the marker. The same results are pushed to the plugin's panel, where the user can filter and tick items off. `truncated: true` means more than 200 matches exist and only the first 200 are returned; `total` then equals the number returned, not the true count. An empty match list is a successful result, not an error. This tool only reads the string it is given: it does not open files, does not modify anything, and makes no network requests.

get_selection.description: Read the panel's state as structured data after the user has triaged it. Returns JSON { hasScan, lastScanAt, filter, total, truncated, visibleCount, unresolvedCount, resolvedCount, byTag, items, markdown, note } where `items` are the still-unresolved markers the panel shows, each { key, line, column, tag, text }, and `markdown` is that list as a `- [ ]` checklist ready to paste. `items` and `markdown` follow the active `filter`, as do `visibleCount`, `unresolvedCount` and `resolvedCount`: `visibleCount` is what the panel shows, `resolvedCount` counts items the user actually ticked, and markers hidden by the filter are never counted as resolved. `total` and `byTag` describe the whole scan, not the filtered view. If `truncated` is true the scan stopped at the 200-marker cap and the list is incomplete — `note` says so. Call this when the user refers to what they ticked or filtered in the panel. It performs no I/O: it reads the last scan held in memory. If hasScan is false, ask the user to run a scan first.
